AA · T09 · timing rule · pre-registration sha256 30973068e5cd · data: APPROVED_DATA.md as of 2026-11-12

Do the three-index switch, with a fixed 50/50 sleeve and with a MAUc1-timed GOLDBEES sleeve, still choose when to hold the portfolio better than chance on a three-index proxy portfolio, 2011-11-25 → 2019-01-02, before the parents' holdings exist?

2011-11-25 → 2019-01-02 · four proxy books (the names only label four band mixes) · decisions every Friday, trades next session at OHLC4 · 10.4 bps a side · 2,000 draws per book, cost and null · every number is computed from evidence/headline/

The answer

On this stretch with a proxy portfolio: the fixed-50/50 rule does not clear the pass mark against random in-or-out timing (A1 or A2 fails); the MAUc1-timed rule does not clear the pass mark against random in-or-out timing (C1 or C2 fails); the MAUc1 timing of the sleeve is not distinguishable from random gold timing (C3 or C4 fails). The proxy portfolio holds the Nifty 100, Midcap 100 and Smallcap 100 at each book's fixed mix (reset at the start of every quarter while held) only when the three weekly supertrends are all BUY, and otherwise a sleeve of GOLDBEES and cash: 50/50 in Part A, and 80/20 when the weekly MAUc1 gold supertrend is BUY and 20/80 when it is SELL in Part B. Judged against random timings on 2011-11-25 → 2019-01-02, after 20.8 bps. A1 (return) and A2 (worst fall) of the 50/50 rule against F1 run with the 50/50 sleeve: 0 of 4 books and 0 of 4 at the 90th percentile (pre-registered pass: 3 of 4 each); F2 beside: 0 and 0. C1 and C2, the timed rule against F1 (real MAUc1 signal in every draw): 0 of 4 and 0 of 4; F2 beside: 0 and 0. C3 and C4, the gold timing against F3 (real in-or-out switch): 0 of 4 and 0 of 4; F4 beside: 0 and 0. Holm-adjusted p-values (m = 6) are in the table.

The catch: the window starts 2011-11-25, before the parents' holdings exist, and the portfolio is a proxy that no investor held; its mixes come from the parents' 2019-2026 holdings. The rule, its weights and the signals were chosen after the 2014-2026 results were seen; only 2011-11-25 → 2014-06-30 predates that look, and the GOLDBEES leg before 2014-07-01 is a MAUc1-based proxy. Every three-index and MAUc1 row is a backfill by the production code. On the window starting 2012-01-02 (R3) the 50/50 rule, the timed rule and the gold timing clear the 90th percentile in 0, 0 and 0 of 4 books. Every result here is in-sample and PROVISIONAL.

Percentile = share of the 2,000 draws the rule beats (ties count half). Pass mark: 90 in at least 3 of 4 books, against the deciding null (F1 for A1, A2, C1, C2, with the 50/50 sleeve in the draws for A1 and A2; F3 for C3 and C4). Holm p = Holm-adjusted p-value over the six criteria (m = 6) of that book (the pass mark is on the unadjusted percentile). After 20.8 bps round-trip cost. Window 2011-11-25 → 2019-01-02. The four books have the same in-or-out decisions and the same gold series and share their draws, so "3 of 4" is a consistency check, not four tests.

What to be careful about

  • Each null randomises one timing and holds the other real. F1 and F2 move the in-or-out switch and read the real gold signal in whatever weeks they are OUT (with the sleeve fixed at 50/50 for A1 and A2); F3 and F4 keep the real switch and move the gold signal. A pass says the rule's timing beats random placement of that one ingredient, not that it beats holding the portfolio. Both random together is only a robustness check (R5).
  • Only C3 and C4 bear on the gold timing. A1 and A2 replicate T06 and C1 and C2 replicate T08 on a different stretch and a proxy. The gold nulls move only the sleeve's split, so their spread is narrower than F1's (see the power tables).
  • Nothing is out of sample. The rule, the 80/20 weights and MAUc1 were chosen after seeing 2014-2026 results; the stretch 2011-11-25 → 2014-06-30 predates that look but its decisions are a backfill by the production code, as is every MAUc1 row. On the window starting 2012-01-02, the 50/50 rule, the timed rule and the gold timing clear the 90th percentile in 0, 0 and 0 of 4 books.
  • 12 round trips and 11 sleeve trades per book is all the evidence there is. The smallest return edge detectable at 80% power against F1 (timed) is 11.7 to 13.8 pp a year; against F3 3.5 to 3.5 pp.
  • The books are one market. SCMO_0007's return percentile for the timed rule against F1 is 60.5 and against F3 56.8.

The data

The proxy portfolio is three raw indices (price indices, no dividends), the Nifty 100, Midcap 100 and Smallcap 100, held at fixed weights per book and filled at the (open+high+low+close)/4 of each index's daily bar (D25, copied from production's index file). The calendar is D26's. The three weekly index signals are D03's Master files; the Smallcap 100 rows are read from 2011-11-25 and its prices from 2011-11-25 (standing rule 7: its prices before 2011-10-03 are corrupt). The gold signal is the weekly SIGN of MAUc1, MCX gold futures, recomputed from the start of the export (D24b). The GOLDBEES leg is GOLDBEES from 2014-07-01 (D09) and a MAUc1-based proxy before (D09b). Cash is the LBES level. Every file below is an APPROVED row of data/APPROVED_DATA.md, whose "As of" date is 2026-11-12 (the run recorded 2026-11-12). No price after 2019-01-02 is read, and no stock, basket or published NAV.

Caveats, disclosed: (1) the proxy is not a book anyone held: the mixes are 2019-2026 averages, the indices are price indices with no tracking error or dividends, and fills at an index's OHLC4 at 10.4 bps a side are an assumption; there is no check of the proxy against the real parents in this test. (2) The GOLDBEES leg before 2014-07-01 is a MAUc1 proxy that tracks GOLDBEES only loosely (the correlations are in T09.md section 2); MAUc1 is a futures series with roll artifacts; R7 re-runs the rule with two variants of the proxy leg. (3) The LBES file's source before 2026-08-10 is unrecorded (F-AA-D09); LIQUIDCASE cash (R2) cannot change a number in this window. (4) Decisions are a backfill by the production code, and so is every MAUc1 row. (5) The rule, its weights and the signals were chosen after seeing 2014-2026 results. (6) The Smallcap 100 prices before 2011-10-03 and its signal before 2011-11-25 are not read.

Amendments before the run (outside the frozen sections of T09.md; found while the engine was built, before any NAV or return of a run was read):

  1. Trade arithmetic. §3 step 6 says the post-cost targets "solve the fixed point exactly (…the engine's trade() solves them)". That is wrong about T06 and T08. Their trade(), which the T09 engine and verifier follow, computes the value traded at the pre-cost targets, charges cost = ow × traded, and then scales every target by (V − cost) ÷ V. So after a sleeve rebalance or a reset the post-trade values equal the targets × (V − cost) ÷ V exactly, but the cost is on the pre-cost trade, not on a fixed point. V6 checks this form.
  2. Saturday sessions. §3 (calendar sentence and contaminants table) says D26 omits Saturday special sessions that the index files contain. The D25 copies (taken from production's file) contain none, so no row is dropped; the Saturday sessions are in Manu's INDTradingDays.xlsx, which this test does not read.
  3. Gold bars. §3 step 1 asserts a GOLDBEES bar on every session. The session 2016-10-30 (an NSE session) has none in D09, so the engine carries the previous close and fill and counts it. Three sessions (2014-10-23, 2015-01-01, 2015-11-11) have no MCX range in D24b's daily file and are filled at the raw GOLDBEES OHLC4.
  4. Gold flips "while IN". §2 counts 15 flips "while the rule is IN (no trade)"; one of them falls on an entry decision (OUT → IN). It is no trade either way.
  5. R2. LIQUIDCASE cash equals LBES to 1.6e-10 in daily return on this window, so R2 cannot change any number; it is reported as a null result.
  6. Readings (all in audit.json): a quarterly reset trades only if the book holds the proxy at the start of the session and no decision trade falls on it, and a reset on the window's last session (2019-01-02, which opens a quarter) is traded; F1 and F2 draws in the fixed 50/50 mode are run at all three costs (R1 needs A1 and A2 at 0 and 50 bps); R7(b) holds the gold weight at 0.5 for decisions dated before 2014-07-01; V5(a)'s chi-square uses the seed of T06 and T08 ([6, 123456789]), and the same test with a first element 12 gives p = 0.0031, which also passes, so both are reported.

One backtest, end to end (SCMO_0003, 20.8 bps, 2011-11-25 → 2019-01-02)

1. The decision. On Friday 2012-05-04 (week 23) the latest weekly rows of the three index files read Nifty 100 BUY, Midcap 100 SELL, Smallcap 100 BUY, and the latest MAUc1 row (2012-05-04) reads BUY. Not all three index signals are BUY, so the target is the sleeve, split 80% GOLDBEES / 20% cash because MAUc1 is BUY (Part A would split it 50/50); last week the book held the proxy portfolio.

state(d) = IN if SIGN_Nifty100 = SIGN_MC100 = SIGN_SC100 = BUY (latest row dated on or before d), else OUT g(d) = SIGN of the latest MAUc1 row dated on or before d w(d) = 0.8 if g(d) = BUY, 0.2 if SELL IN → Nifty 100 / Midcap 100 / Smallcap 100 at (0.09626177, 0.19679459, 0.70694364), reset on entry and at the first session of each quarter OUT → w(d) GOLDBEES + (1 − w(d)) cash (changed only when the target changes)

2. The exit trade. On the next session, 2012-05-07, at the (open+high+low+close)/4 of every instrument the book sells the three index positions and buys GOLDBEES and cash. Value before: 1.034031; value traded (both sides): 2.068062; cost = traded × 20.8 ÷ 2 ÷ 10,000 = 0.002151. After the trade GOLDBEES is worth 0.825504 and cash 0.206376, that is 80.00% in GOLDBEES (target 80% of the value after cost, 1.031880). The GOLDBEES fill is the proxy's OHLC4 (the session is before 2014-07-01). NAV at the close after the trade: 1.029059.

10. How one F1 draw is made. It keeps the 12 in-spells and 13 out-spells, the first state (out) and the totals (172 weeks in, 200 out), and draws every length as an integer from 1 to 32 (in) or 2 to 35 (out; each bound is the series' own: the lower is min(2, shortest spell of the state), the upper its longest spell), every allowed set of lengths equally likely. With c(m, t) the number of ways to write t weeks as m lengths in the bounds, c(0, 0) = 1 and c(m, t) = Σ over x of c(m − 1, t − x), the parts are drawn one at a time: with m parts and t weeks left, P(length = x) = c(m − 1, t − x) ÷ c(m, t). The uniform number u is rng.random() and the length is the first x whose cumulative weight exceeds u × c(m, t). In-spell parts come first, then out-spell parts, from the same generator. The real MAUc1 signal is then read in whatever weeks the draw is OUT; for A1 and A2 the same states are run with the sleeve fixed at 50/50.

The comparators are benchmarks, not nulls. Hold the proxy: the engine with the decision fixed IN (quarterly resets). The constant mixes hold the rule's average share (46.2%, invested weeks ÷ weeks) in the proxy portfolio all the time and rebalance at every decision, with a 50/50 non-proxy share and with a MAUc1-timed one; the 100% sleeves are the other end; the 50/50-sleeve rule is Part A's rule, so the gap to the timed rule is the sleeve's effect; each single index is held with no resets. There is no published-NAV comparator (the parents' NAVs start on 2019-01-02).

MDE = 2.8 × the SD of the draws (80% power, two-sided 5%), per null. The numbers did not exist when the pre-registration was written; its thresholds do not depend on them.

Definitions

  • Percentile: (draws worse + 0.5 × draws tied) ÷ draws × 100, ties equal within a relative 1e-12. p-value: (1 + draws at least as good) ÷ (draws + 1). Holm p: the Holm step-down adjustment of the six deciding p-values of a book.
  • CAGR: NAV_end^(252 ÷ (sessions − 1)) − 1, daily NAV, after cost. Worst fall (maximum drawdown): the most negative NAV ÷ running peak − 1.
  • Proxy portfolio: the Nifty 100, Midcap 100 and Smallcap 100 at a book's fixed weights, reset to those weights on entry and at the first session of each quarter while held. MAUc1: the weekly supertrend (period W, multiplier 2) of MCX gold futures (D24b). Gold signal g: its SIGN, BUY or SELL, from the latest weekly row dated on or before the decision date. Sleeve: while the rule is OUT, GOLDBEES and cash, 50/50 (Part A) or 80/20 when g is BUY and 20/80 when SELL (Part B), changed only when g changes.
  • F1 in-or-out N4.10 with the real gold signal (seed default_rng([12, 6, id])); F2 in-or-out N4.9 spell shuffle ([12, 3, id]); F3 gold N4.10-g with the real switch ([12, 11, 6, id]); F4 gold N4.9-g spell shuffle ([12, 11, 3, id]); F5 an F1 and an F3 draw together (robustness only). F1 and F2 are also run with the sleeve fixed at 50/50 (F1f, F2f in the tables), the nulls of A1 and A2.
  • N4.10 free-length random timing: the same number of spells of each state and the same totals of weeks in each, every length an integer between the series' own bounds for that state, uniform over all allowed ordered tuples, drawn exactly by a dynamic programme, no rejection. N4.9 spell shuffle: the real series' spells of each state reordered among themselves. All nulls start in the real series' first state.
  • Weeks versus sessions: the in-or-out nulls hold invested weeks exactly; a week has 3 to 5 sessions, so invested sessions differ by draw and are reported.
  • MDE: 2.8 × the SD of the draws' CAGR (or maximum drawdown). R3 window: 2012-01-02 → 2019-01-02.
